intervention.definition: F8 -> 7x6 average pool over channels (42) + channel-and-row mean per column (24) + channel-and-column mean per row (28) = 94, then Linear(94,256) initialised at exactly zero; arm A bypasses the layer and keeps it frozen at zero
intervention.private_calls: backbone._checked_regions, backbone._playfield_input and backbone.playfield are called in the same order forward_core calls them; a unit test recomputes forward_core's tail from the extracted F4/F8 and asserts bitwise equality

resolution.note: the F8 column axis is the screen-x axis: 192 model columns / 24 = 8 model px per column, i.e. 16 native playfield px, so a 12-20 px gap is about one F8 column wide and the frozen vector is coarse by construction

intervention.head: SpatialHead: TacticalPolicy.forward_features with the input `features` detach removed and nothing else
intervention.note: the only change against round21 is the fusion layer between the frozen trunk features and the same N1 head; A is round21 A

storage.dtype: uint8 (the renderer output verbatim, never cast to float on disk)
storage.container: npz deflate for the pixel regions, torch.save (xb) for history/labels
storage.scale: uint8 -> float32 /255 happens only at load through vision.regions_to_batch
storage.hud: hud_score/hud_status are byte-identical across all 80 decisions (asserted per event); stored once as [1,3,H,W,C] and expanded to 80 rows at load, so the values are identical while the 80 redundant copies are not written
storage.why: a float32 copy of the same content is 4x larger and adds nothing: every consumer divides by 255 immediately

data.spatial_definition: F8 [B,96,28,24] -> 42 (7x6 pool over channels) + 24 (column profile) + 28 (row profile) = 94 float32 per decision row, produced by the same frozen backbone pass that produced features/base

equivalence.step0: unit tested: identical policy logits and identical masked action at step 0

flip.method: each stored closed-loop trajectory is re-rendered from its own x trace and replayed; at every decision inside the telegraph window the same network state also sees the playfield mirrored horizontally (hud untouched) and the two masked argmax screen actions are compared

prediction.note: the masked argmax actually taken, from the stored rows; per event, over all 80 decisions and over the telegraph-window decisions only

base_bias.note: the frozen baseline (B0) is the same backbone policy head the residual offset is built on; its per-decision screen preference on the identical telegraph renders is the base prior this round is testing against

design.rows: decisions whose logical frame 2*i is inside [max(0, wall_frame-45), wall_frame)
design.fit: F1 train events only (6 events, 3 groups, base + mirror)

ridge.folds: leave one F1 train group out
ridge.note: lambda=1.0 is the headline value; the sweep is reported so the conclusion does not depend on that one choice (measured: the ordering of the two representations is the same across seven orders of magnitude)

design.targets: screen px: gap side, gap centre, gap centre minus the player x
design.note: read-only measurement of the frozen representation; it trains nothing and reads no validation pixel

symmetry.note: the column profile of m0 against the reversed column profile of m1 on the same group; the F8 column axis is the screen-x axis, so a layout-reading backbone must be close to mirror-symmetric here

design.rows: all 80 decision rows of the 14 train events, on the stored frozen vectors; read-only
design.note: constant = projection(mean spatial vector); conditioning = delta - constant. Both arms are otherwise identical, so this separates "the fusion re-biased the head" from "the fusion conditioned it on the screen"

ablation.method: the trained S checkpoint is rerun with `fusion.enabled = False` (the delta is bypassed, no parameter changes, no retraining) on the six F1 holdout events; feasibility, first hit, direction and parking error are then recomputed the same way
ablation.caveat: the S head weights were trained *with* the delta, so "delta off" is a counterfactual probe of what the delta does, not arm A

probes.replay_note: the flip probe also reports replay fidelity: the fraction of steps on which the rebuilt stack reproduces the stored masked argmax, i.e. that the probe sees the runner inputs

round21_reference.f1_deaths: round21: every F1 death (validation 24 + train 27 + B0 12) is on wall_frame

comparison.note: three seed pairs, six F1 validation events each; S minus A; descriptive only

limitations: n=3 seeds and 7 validation groups; the 14 validation events collapse to 7 geometries because a mirror is not an independent sample
F2 validation is a single group (2 events), so an F2 validation number is not a rate
the intervention is a 94-d pooled view of a 28x24 map: one F8 column is 16 native px, so a 12-20 px gap is about one column wide and the vector is coarse by construction
the fusion layer is the only trained addition; the frozen backbone and the head geometry are round20
the F1 win condition is exact parking inside a 12-20 px gap; it is not tactical understanding
synthetic fixed-y worlds, two-frame actions, no shot, no bomb, no real TH08 pixels
research heads only: no formal gate, no deployable checkpoint, no game
